FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Water Quality for Industrial Purposes Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division 
Council. 


Improvement in the quality of potable water supply is a thrust area of all municipal and Public Health Engineering 
Department water supply systems. As part of this quest to improve the quality of water supplied, there is a need for 
most cost effective and efficient water treatment chemicals. 


Polyaluminium chloride is an effective coagulant used to remove microscopic suspended matter quickly over a 
wide range of turbidity, temperature and pH as encountered in natural surface waters. It is also effective for 
removing algae. Polyaluminium chloride (PAC) is a general name given to polyaluminium chloride compounds, 
namely polyaluminium chloride hydroxide and polyaluminium chloride hydroxide sulphate, general chemical 
formula of which is mentioned below alongwith CAS No: 


Chemical Formula CAS No. 

[Al (OH), Cl,],, a=2.5,b=0.5 12042-91-0 

(n = 15) and a=2, b=1 10284-64-7 
a and b variable 1327-41-9 
(a > 1.05) 

[A1 (OH),Cl, (SO,).], a, b and c variable 

(n = 15) a> 1.05 39290-78-3 


This standard was first published in year 2005. In this revision, all amendments are included and the requirements 
for selenium and total organic carbon alongwith the method of tests have been incorporated. The limit of Chloride 
requirement in the medium Basicity powder grade PAC has been modified. The Basicity characteristic has been 
renamed in line with international practices, as “Relative basicity”. ICP Method for determination of heavy metal 
has also been incorporated as an alternate method. 


Further, the requirements for raw material is also incorporated by specifying that Polyaluminium chloride is to be 
manufactured from virgin raw materials (which are not by-products of any industry) so that it is safe for drinking 
water. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

POLYALUMINIUM CHLORIDE 
(First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the characteristics, 
requirements, and methods of sampling and test for 
polyaluminium chloride liquid and powder. 


2 REFERENCES

3 GRADES 


The material shall be in the form of liquid or powder, 
each of two types: (a) Medium basicity, and (b) High 
basicity, both grades are effective coagulant for the 
treatment of low to high turbidity surface raw water 
for drinking purposes. 


4 RAW MATERIALS 


Polyaluminium chloride is to be manufactured from 
virgin raw materials (which are not by-products of any 
industry) so that it is safe for drinking water. 


5 REQUIREMENTS 


5.1 Description 
5.1.1 For Liquid 


Polyaluminium chloride shall be colorless to pale 
yellow, hazy to transparent liquid and shall be free from 
organic contaminants [see SI No. (ix) of Table 1]. 


5.1.2 For Powder 


Polyaluminium chloride powder shall be in the form 
of pale yellow powder and shall be free from organic 
contaminants [see S1 No. (ix) of Table 1]. 


5.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements specified in Table 1, when tested by 
methods specified in col 7 and 8 of Table 1. The quantity 
of the sample taken for various tests is for liquid 
material product. For powder material product it shall 
be one-third of the quantity of liquid material taken for 
tests. Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be used in tests. 


6 PACKING, MARKING AND STORAGE 


6.1 Packing 


The liquid material shall be packed or transported in 
acid resistant rubber or HDPE or plastic lined 
containers, tankers or tank car. The powder material 
shall be packed in laminated HDPE bags with inner 
polyethylene liner/ liners securely tied or sealed to avoid 
absorption of moisture during transport/storage, or as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 
Polyaluminium chloride powder absorbs moisture when 
exposed to atmosphere.

6.2 Marking 


The containers shall bear legibly and indelibly the 
following information: 


a) Name and grade of the material; 

b) Name ofthe manufacturer and trade-mark, if 
any; 

c) Mass ofthe material in package or tanker; 

d) Date of manufacture; and 

e) Batch No./Lot No. 


6.2.1 If the material is supplied in bulk, a card bearing 
all the information required as mentioned in 6.2 shall 
be placed with the supply. 


6.2.2 The container shall also be marked with the 
following information: 


Corrosive liquid, irritating to eyes; in case of contact, 
rinse immediately with plenty of water and seek medical 
advice. On contact with skin, wash immediately with 
plenty of water, immediately take off all the 
contaminated clothing. Wear suitable gloves and eyes 
and face protection devices, while handling the material. 


6.2.3 BIS Certification Marking 


The packages may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


6.2.3.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which the licence for 
the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


6.3 Storage 


The liquid material shall be stored in dark colour acid 
proof rubber/FRP/PP lined/STP tanks under shade (to 
avoid direct sunlight). Solid material to be stored in a 
covered dry place. 


7 SAMPLING 


Representative samples of the material shall be drawn 
and their conformity to this standard shall be determined 
in accordance with method prescribed in Annex T. 


IS 15573 : 2018 


ANNEX A 
[Table 1, S1 No. (i)] 
DETERMINATION OF ALUMINIUM OXIDE 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


A-1.1 Total aluminium in sample solution is converted 
to Al** ions by addition of dilute nitric acid and heating, 
followed by complexation of Al** with an excess of 
ethylenediamine tetra acetic acid disodium (EDTA) 
solution. Excess EDTA is titrated with a standard 
volumetric solution of zinc in the presence of xylenol 
orange as indicator. 


AB+EDTA* — AIEDTA™ 
Zn?*+EDTA* > Zn EDTA? 


A-1.2 Reagents 
A-1.2.1 Nitric Acid (1 : 12) 


A-1.2.2 M/20 EDTA — Dissolve about 19 g of 
ethylenediamine tetra acetic acid disodium salt 
dihydrate in distilled water, transfer to a 1000 ml 
volumetric flask and make up to the mark by distilled 
water and shake well. 


A-1.2.3 Sodium Acetate Buffer Solution — Dissolve 
272 g of sodium acetate- trihydrate in 500 ml water 
and add glacial acetic acid until pH of solution become 
5.5+0.1. Transfer the solution to 1-litre volumetric 
flask and makeup the volume to | litre. 


A-1.2.4 Xylenol Orange Indicator 


a) Solution, 0.1 percent (w/v) — Dissolve 0.1 g 
of xylenol orange powder in about 70 ml water, 
shake and make up to 100 ml. Shake well. 

b) Powder, xylenol orange mixture (1 percent w/w 
in potassium nitrate). Grind 1.0 g of xylenol 
orange with 99 g of potassium nitrate in a mortar 
until a homogeneous material is obtained. 

A-1.2.5 Hydrochloric Acid — AR grade (see IS 265). 


A-1.2.6 M/50 Zinc Solution — Weigh accurately 1.308 
g of AR grade zinc metal pellets/granule and transfer 
to a 250 ml beaker, add 15ml of water and 6-7 ml of 
concentrated hydrochloric acid AR and cover with 
watch glass, heat to dissolve zinc, evaporate on a water 
bath nearly to dryness, dissolve the residue in water 
and transfer the contents quantitatively into a 1 000 ml 
volumetric flask and make up to the mark.

M, = molarity of zinc solution, and 


m = mass of zinc metal taken for preparation of 
solution. 


A-1.3 Procedure 


A-1.3.1 Weigh accurately to the nearest | mg of PAC 
sample (for powder about 2.5 g and for liquid about 
7 g) ina weighing bottle. Transfer it quantitatively to a 
500 ml volumetric flask with aid of about 150 ml water, 
dissolve by shaking and make up to mark. 


A-1.3.2 Pipette out accurately 20 ml of this solution to 
a 250 ml conical flask, add 2 ml of nitric acid (1:12) (the 
pH value shall be between 1 to 2), boil for 1 min, allow 
to cool and add 20 ml of M/20 EDTA solution exactly. 


A-1.3.3 Adjust to pH 3 with nitric acid or 10 percent 
sodium hydroxide solution using pH meter or by thymol 
blue pH test paper. Boil for about 2 min. 


A-1.3.4 Cool and add approximately 10 ml sodium 
acetate buffer solution (pH of mixture should be 
5.5 + 0.1), add 2 to 5 drops of xylenol orange solution 
or add 30-50 mg | percent (w/v) xylenol orange mixture 
in potassium nitrate (A-1.2.4). 


A-1.3.5 Titrate the solution with M/50 zinc solution until 
the colour of the solution changes from pale yellow colour 
to pale red indicating reaching of end point. Note down 
the volume of the zinc solution consumed during titration. 


A-1.3.6 In parallel, pipette out 20 ml M/20 EDTA, add 
2 ml of nitric acid (1:12) solution to a 250 ml conical 
flask, add about 20 ml distilled water and proceed the 
test as described in A-1.3.3 to A-1.3.5 for blank.

ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. (ii)] 
DETERMINATION OF RELATIVE BASICITY 


B-1 PRINCIPLE 


Sample solution is depolymerized by heating in acidic 
medium. Potassium fluoride is added to complex 
aluminium. Excess of acid is titrated with standard 
alkali using phenolphthalein as an indicator. 


B-1.1 Reagents 


B-1.1.1 Potassium Fluoride Solution [50 percent (w/v) ] 
— Dissolve 250 g of anhydrous potassium fluoride in 
water to 500 ml and filter through a filter paper. Store 
the solution in plastic bottle (PE/PP bottle/flask). 


B-1.1.2 Non-carbonic Water — Boil redistilled water 
for 2 min to remove CO, - gas and volatile components 
and allow to cool to room temperature, preventing from 
the absorption of CO, - gas in the air. 


B-1.1.3 Ethyl Alcohol Solution of Methyl Red- 
Bromocresol Green — Dissolve 0.02 g of methyl red 
and 0.1 g of bromocresol green in 100 ml ethyl alcohol 
[95 percent (w/v)| 


B-1.1.4 Ethyl Alcohol Solution of Phenolphthalein 
[0.5 percent (w/v)| — Dissolve 0.5 g of phenolphthalein 
in 100 ml of ethyl alcohol [50 percent (v/v)], add sodium 
hydroxide solution (N/50) drop by drop until the colour 
of the solution turns slightly pink. 


B-1.1.5 Sodium Carbonate (Anhydrous) — AR grade. 
B-1.1.6 Sodium Hydroxide — AR grade. 


B-1.1.7 Hydrochloric Acid Solution (N/2) — Transfer 
40 to 45 ml conc hydrochloric acid (AR grade) to a 
1 000 ml volumetric flask and make upto the mark with 
distilled water, shake well and standardize this solution 
as follows. 


B-1.1.7.1 Standardization — Sodium carbonate 
(anhydrous) of 99.9 percent purity contains a little 
moisture, which is to be dehydrated by heating at 260- 
270°C for half an hour and allow to cool in dessicator 
before use. Weigh out accurately from a weighing bottle 
about 0.5 to 0.7 g of sodium carbonate into a 250 ml 
conical flask. Dissolve it in 20 ml distilled water 
(see B-1.1.2) and add some drops of methyl red- 
bromocresol green (see B-1.1.3), titrate with 
hydrochloric acid until the colour of solution turns from 
blue to purplish red indicating reaching of end point. 
Note down the volume of HCl consumed during 
titration. Calculate normality of HCl as follows:

B-1.1.8 Sodium Hydroxide Solution (N/2) — Add 
about 100 g of sodium hydroxide gradually in 250 ml 
conical flask (Stoppard) with about 100 ml of water, 
with care of generating heat, allow to dissolve with 
agitating by glass rod, prepare the saturated solution, 
allow to stand till over night with stopper, and dilute 
about 20 ml of supernatant liquid with non-carbonic 
acid water (see B-1.1.2) to 1 000 ml. Standardize this 
solution as follows. 


B-1.1.8.1 Standardization — Pipette out exactly 25 ml 
of N/2 hydrochloric acid (see B-1.1.7) to a conical flask, 
and after adding 2 to 3 drops of phenolphthalein 
solution (B-1.1.4), titrate it with sodium hydroxide 
solution until the colour of the solution turns to pink, 
indicates reaching of end point. Note down the volume 
of NaOH solution consumed during the titration.

B-1.2 Procedure 


B-1.2.1 Weigh about 2 g of the liquid/solid sample in a 
beaker accurately to the nearest 1 mg and dissolve in 
20-30 ml of water in a 250 ml conical flask. 


B-1.2.2 Pipette out precisely 25 ml of hydrochloric acid 
solution (N/2) and add to the sample, cover with a watch 
glass, after heating for 10 min on a water bath, cool to 
room temperature and add at once 25 ml of potassium 
fluoride solution [50 percent (w/) ]. 


B-1.2.3 Add about 5 drops of phenolphthalein 
solution (B-1.1.4) and immediately titrate with N/2 
sodium hydroxide solution until the colour of the 
solution turns to pink, indicating reaching of end point.

ANNEX C 


[Table 1, SI No. (iii )] 
LONG TERM PROTECTION TEST 


C-1 PRINCIPLE 


Acidified sample solution is titrated with standard 
mercuric nitrate solution using mixed diphenyl- 
carbazone and bromophenol blue indicator. The end 
point is shown by the formation of the blue violet 
mercury diphenylcarbazone complex. 


C-1.1 Reagents 


C-1.1.1 Nitric Acid — Mix 3 volumes of concentrated 
nitric acid (sp gr 1.42) with 997 volumes of distilled 
water. 


C-1.1.2 Mixed Indicator Solution — Dissolve 0.5 g of 
crystalline diphenylcarbazone and 0.5 g of 
bromophenol blue powder in 100m1 of methyl alcohol 
(95 percent). Store in a brown bottle and replace after 
every 6 months. 


C-1.1.3 Standard Sodium Chloride Solution (0.1 N) 
— Weigh accurately about 5.844 g (AR/GR) of sodium 
chloride (previously dried at 105°C for 2 h and cooled 
in dessicator), transfer to 1 000 ml volumetric flask 
with the help of distilled water and make up the volume 
to the mark with distilled water. 


W 
Normality of sodium chloride solution, n 58.44 
C-1.1.4 Mercuric Nitrate Solution (0.1 N) — Dissolve 
17.130 g of mercuric nitrate monohydrate in 50 ml of 
acidified water [5:1 ratio of water /concentrated nitric 
acid (sp gr 1.42)]. Dilute the acidified mercuric nitrate 
solution with distilled water to 1 litre. 


C-1.1.5 Standardization of Mercuric Nitrate Solution 
(0.1 N) — Take 25 ml of standard 0.1 N sodium 
chloride solution in a 250 ml conical flask, dilute with 
distilled water, add 5 to 10 drops of mixed indicator 
solution, add 2 to 3 drops of dilute nitric acid (3 : 997) 
and titrate it with 0.1 N mercuric nitrate 
solution (C-1.1.4) till colour turns from yellow to blue 
violet, indicates reaching of end point. Note down the 
volume of mercuric nitrate solution consumed in titration.

consumed in titration, in ml. 


C-1.2 Procedure 


Weigh accurately to nearest 1 mg accuracy of the 
sample (for liquid 5g, solid 1.7g) in a 100 ml beaker 
and dissolve it in approximately 30 ml of water, transfer 
it completely in to a 500 ml volumetric flask using

nitrate solution, until the colour of solution turns to 
blue-violet, indicates reaching of end point. Record the 
volume (say V ml) of mercuric nitrate solution 
consumed in titration.

ANNEX D 


[Table 1, SI No. (iv)] 
DETERMINATION OF SULPHATE 


D-1 PRINCIPLE 


Sulphate in solution is determined gravimetrically by 
precipitation as barium sulphate in acidic medium. 


D-1.1 Reagents 


D-1.1.1 Hydrochloric Acid Solution — Approximately 
4N. 


D-1.1.2 Barium Chloride Solution — 10 percent (w/v). 


D-1.2 Procedure 


Weigh accurately to nearest Img of the sample (for 
liquid about 10 g, for solid about 2.5 g) and transfer to 
a 250 ml beaker and dissolve in about 100 ml of water. 
Adjust the pH to 2.0-2.5 by drop-wise addition of the 
hydrochloric acid solution (D-1.1.1) and heat to boil. 
Add 10-12 ml of barium chloride solution drop by drop 


to the boiling solution so that the addition is in slight 
excess and continue boiling for 4-5 min to obtain a 
granular precipitate. Allow to stand for 4 h and filter 
through a weighed sintered glass crucible G-4, under 
suction. Wash the precipitate repeatedly with hot water 
(at 60-70°C) until the filtrate is chloride free on testing 
with silver nitrate solution. Dry to constant mass at 105- 
110°C and weigh. 


D-1.3 Calculation 


(M, —M,)x 41.154 
M 


Percent sulphate (as SO,) 
where 


M, = mass of empty crucible, in g; 
M, = mass of crucible with BaSO,, in g; and 


M = mass of sample taken, in g. 


IS 15573 : 2018 


ANNEX E 
[Table 1, SI No. (v)] 
DETERMINATION OF SPECIFIC GRAVITY 


E-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


Specific gravity of liquid PAC is evaluated by specific 
gravity hydrometer at 25°C temperature. In case of 
dispute, specific gravity shall be determined by 
Pyknometer method as per IS 3506. 


E-1.1 Apparatus 


E-1.1.1 Specific Gravity Hydrometer — The 
hydrometer shall be of scale range 1.1-1.3 (effective 
scale range 1.150 to 1.250). 


E-1.1.2 Cylinder — The cylinder shall be made of glass, 
having no distortion which may disturb the reading of 
hydrometer and its size shall be such that when the 
hydrometer is floated in the cylinder, the distance 
between any part of the hydrometer and the inner wall 
or the bottom surface of cylinder shall be not less than 
1 cm. 


E-1.1.3 Thermometer — Glass mercurial thermometer 
shall be of scale range — 10 to 110°C, L.C.-0.5°C. 


E-1.2 Procedure 


Clean the hydrometer and cylinder thoroughly before 
use so as to show the clear meniscus. Proper amount of 
sample shall be transferred into the cylinder and kept 
at 25°C to attain the temperature. After mixing sample 
completely with an agitating rod, pick up the upper end 
of the hydrometer, float it on the liquid gently so as it 
does not adhere any bubbles. After stabilizing the 
flotation of the hydrometer, same is push down to sink 
further to approximately 2 scale marks in the sample 
and release gently. After stabilizing the float of the 
hydrometer, read the scale adopting upper edge of the 
meniscus. Repeat this measurement 2 to 3 times and 
the average value of the readings gives the specific 
gravity of the liquid. 


NOTES 

1 Differences between each measured value to average value 
shall not be more than the value corresponds to one scale 
interval. 

2 Any air circulation through electrical fan should be avoided 
in surrounding area while performing the test. 


ANNEX F 
[Table 1, SI No. (vii)] 
BULK DENSITY 


F-1 PRINCIPLE 

Measured volume of powder sample is weighed and 
expressed weight per unit volume. 

F-1.1 Apparatus 

F-1.1.1 Rubber Base Pad 

F-1.1.2 Funnel — Glass funnel of 12.5 mm diameter. 
F-1.1.3 Cylinder — Stoppered measuring glass 
cylinder, marked capacity- 100ml, 1.c.-1ml. 

F-1.2 Procedure 


Pour the powder sample gently and smoothly in the 
Stoppered measuring cylinder through a funnel, upto 
100 ml mark (without taping/knocking or squeezing). 
Close the cylinder with stopper. Gently lift the cylinder 
upto 50 mm height (from cylinder base to surface) and 
allow it to drop vertically and freely on rubber base pad. 


Repeat the lifting and dropping procedure of the cylinder 
for 50 times. Care shall be taken so that sample from 
cylinder shall not spill out during dropping of cylinder. 


After completion of 50 drops, level the inside material 
of the cylinder with help of narrow head spatula without 
any tapping/ knocking and read the volume of material. 
Also weigh the mass of inside material of the cylinder. 


F-1.3 Calculation 


; M 
Bulk density, g/ml = y 


where 
M = mass ofthe material taken for the test, in g; 
and 
V = volume ofthe material in cylinder after 50 
taps, in ml. 


IS 15573 : 2018 


ANNEX G 
[Table 1, SI No. (viii) (a)] 
DETERMINATION OF MERCURY 


G-1 MERCURY ANALYZER METHOD 


G-1.0 Outline of the Method 


Mercury analyzer works on the principle of cold 
vapour atomic absorption spectrometry technique. 
Mercury ions are reduced to elemental state by 
stannous chloride and the solution is stirred vigorously 
so that equilibrium is achieved between the mercury 
in the solution and air phase. The vapour is then purged 
into the absorption cell which is located in the light 
path of spectrometer. 


As the cold vapour absorption technique of mercury is 
based on absorption of UV radiation (wave length- 
253.7 nm) by mercury atoms, all substances which 
absorb UV radiation will cause the positive error. 
Vapors of organic compounds like alcohols, ketones, 
esters, acids and water also absorb UV radiation. These 
can be avoided with suitable traps provided along with 
the instrument. 


G-1.1 Apparatus 


G-1.1.1 Mercury Analyzer — Based on cold vapour 
atomic absorption spectrometry technique. 


G-1.2 Reagents 


G-1.2.1 Nitric Acid — 10 percent, 5 percent and 
2 percent (v/v). 


G-1.2.2 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid (see IS 265) 


G-1.2.3 Stannous Chloride —20 percent (w/v) in 10 
percent hydrochloric acid (v/v). Take 20 g stannous 
chloride in a clean beaker, add 10 ml of concentrated 
hydrochloric acid and dissolve while warming it over 
a hot plate. Boil for one minute, cool and dilute with 
distilled water to make 100 ml. Add 1-2 g of tin metal 
(pellet) after the preparation of the solution. 


G-1.2.4 Potassium Permanganate — 4 percent (w/v) 
in 10 percent sulphuric acid. Dissolve 20 g of potassium 
permanganate in water and add slowly and carefully 
50 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid with continuous 
stirring and cool the resultant solution to room 
temperature. Make up the volume to 500 ml using 
distilled water. 


G-1.2.5 Hydroxylamine Hydrochloride — 10 percent 
(wf). 


G-1.2.6 Mercuric Chloride — AR grade. 


G-1.2.7 Potassium Dichromate — | percent (w/v). 


G-1.3 Preparation of Standard Graph 
G-1.3.1 Preparation of Stock Solution 


Dissolve 0.135 4 g of mercuric chloride AR grade in 
25 ml of 2 percent nitric acid (v/v). Add 1 ml of 
potassium dichromate solution (see G-1.2.7) and make 
up to 100 ml with 2 percent nitric acid (v/v). One ml of 
this stock solution = 1 mg of Hg. 


G-1.3.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Dilute 10 ml of the stock solution (see G-1.3.1) to 
1 000 ml in a volumetric flask (stock solution — B) so 
that 1 ml of this solution = 10 microgram of Hg. Further, 
pipette out 10 ml of the stock solution — B in another 
volumetric flask andvolume makeup to | 000 ml (stock 
solution — C), so that 1 ml of such stock solution = 0.1 
microgram (100 nanogram) of Hg. For making up the 
dilution of stock solution — C, solution of 5 percent 
nitric acid (v/v) and 0.10 percent potassium 
dichromate (w/v) mix shall be used to make up the final 
volume. This standard solution is generally stable for a 
period of at least a month. 


G-1.3.3 Preparation of Sample 


Weigh accurately about 5 g of the liquid sample (or 
1.7 g of solid sample) in a 50 ml beaker, dissolve the 
sample in 25 ml distilled water and completely transfer 
to a 250 ml volumetric flask with the help of distilled 
water. Add drop-wise potassium permanganate 4 
percent (w/v) solution till purple colour remains, shake 
well and add 2-3 drops of concentrated nitric acid, mix 
thoroughly and keep it for 5-10 min. Decolourize the 
solution by adding drop-wise hydroxylamine 
hydrochloride solution, shake well and make up to the 
mark with distilled water. 


G-1.3.4 Blank Preparation for Calibration 


Transfer 8 ml of 10 percent nitric acid solution and 
2 ml of stannous chloride solution to the reaction vessel 
of Mercury analyzer. Stir it for 5 min. Stop the stirring 
and take the reading for the mercury content, if any in 
the blank, repeat the stirring of the blank solution until 
no deflection/reading is observed. 


G-1.3.5 Procedure for Standard Graph 


Following the procedure explained at G-1.3.4, measure 
optical density/absorbance for various known 
concentration of mercury, that is concentration ranges 
of 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 150 nanograms of 
mercury and plot a standard graph indicating mercury 
in nanograms against optical density. 


G-1.4 Procedure 


Prepare a fresh blank (see G-1.3.4), stir it for 5 min, 
stop the stirring and take reading for the mercury 
content, if any in the blank. Transfer 5 ml of the sample 
solution to the reaction vessel containing blank and 
determine the concentration of the mercury with the 
help of the standard graph (see G-1.3.5). Prepare a 
blank solution using all reagents in same quantities 
except sample in a 250 ml volumetric flask, use distilled 
water in place of sample. Make up to mark with distilled 
water and shake well. Transfer 5 ml of this solution to 
reaction vessel containing blank in the same way as 
sample and calculate mercury content in blank and 


IS 15573 : 2018 


subtract from sample result, and take for calculation 
of mercury content in sample. 


G-1.5 Calculation 
Mercury (as Hg), ppm 


mg of the mercury as Hg in 5 ml sample x 50 x 1000 


Mass of the sample taken for the test, in g 


G-2 ALTERNATE METHOD 


Determine Mercury content by atomic absorption 
spectrophotometer (AAS) with suitable attachment of 
metal hydride system as prescribed in 1S 3025 (Part 48).

referee method. 


H-1.1 Procedure

material) in the minimum amount of distilled water. 
Carry out test for arsenic as per method prescribed 
in 5.1 of IS 2088 by comparison with a stain obtained 
for 0.005 mg of arsenic (as As) [0.009 8 mg of arsenic 
trioxide as As,O,]. 


H-1.2 The limit prescribed in Table | shall be taken 
as not having been exceeded, if the length and intensity 
of the stain is not greater than that produced in the 
control sample. 


H-2 REFEREE METHOD 


By Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer (AAS), 
follow the method as prescribed in IS 3025 (Part 37). 


H-3 ALTERNATE METHOD 


Determine arsenic content by Inductively Coupled 
Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES) as 
prescribed in IS 3025 (Part 2).

ANNEX L 
[Table 1, SI No. (viii) (e)] 
DETERMINATION OF IRON 


L-1 PRINCIPLE 


Iron reacts with thiocyanate to give a series of 
internally red coloured compounds, which remain in 
true solution. Strong acids (hydrochloric acid) should 
be present to reduce hydrolysis of coloured compound 
of Iron. Alternatively Iron may be determined by 
Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer (Referee 
method). 


L-1.1 Reagents 


L-1.1.1 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid — (AR 
Grade, 35-37 percent). 


L-1.1.2 Potassium Permanganate Solution — 
Dissolve 2 g of potassium permanganate solution in 
1 000 ml of distilled water. 


L-1.1.3 Ammonium Thiocyanate Solution — Dissolve 
10 g of ammonium thiocyanate in 100 ml distilled 
water. 


L-1.1.4 Dilute Sulphuric Acid — 1:5. 


L-1.1.5 Standard Iron Solution — (1 ml= 0.1 mg 
Iron) — Standard Iron solution prepared using of 
ferrous ammonium sulphate  hexahydrate 
[FeSO,(NH,),SO,.6 H,O; Molecular weight 392.14]. 
Dissolve 0.702 2 g of AR grade ferrous ammonium 
sulphate hexahydrate in 100m1 of water, add 5 ml of 
dilute sulphuric acid and slowly add a dilute solution 
of potassium permanganate (2 g/1) with continuous 
stirring until a slight pink colour persist. Makeup the 
volume to 1 litre and mix thoroughly. 


L-1.2 Procedure 


Weigh accurately to the nearest 1 mg of sample (for 
liquid about 10 g, for solid about 3.5 g) in a 100 ml 
beaker, add 5 ml concentrated hydrochloric acid, warm 
it and then cool it to room temperature. Transfer it into 
100 ml Nessler cylinder. For blank, take distilled water 
in another Nessler cylinder as a blank. Add 5 ml of 
conc. hydrochloric acid and 3-4 ml of potassium 
permanganate solution, followed by addition of 10 ml 
ammonium thiocyanate to both the cylinders and shake. 


Add distilled water up to the mark. Shake well. Using 
a micro pipette, add standard iron solution (1 ml = 0.1 
mg Fe) to the blank till colour matches with that of 
sample Nessler cylinder. 


L-1.3 Calculation 


Vx100 
Soluble iron compounds as Fe, ppm = 7 
where 
V = volume ofstandard iron solution, in ml; and 
M = mass ofsample taken for the test, in g. 


L-2 REFEREE METHOD 


Determine Iron content by Atomic Absorption 
Spectrophotometer method as given in IS 3025 (Part 53). 


L-3 ALTERNATE METHOD 


Determine iron content by ICP-AES as prescribed in 
IS 3025 (Part 2).

[Table 1, SI No. (viii) (£)] 
DETERMINATION OF MANGANESE 


M-1 PRINCIPLE 


Manganese in sample is oxidized to permanganate (violet 
colour), which is compared visually with standard solution 
ofManganese. Alternatively Mn is determined by Atomic 
Absorption Spectrophotometer (Referee method). 


11 


M-1.1 Apparatus 

M-1.1.1 Nessler Cylinder, 100 ml capacity. 
M-1.2 Reagent 

M-1.2.1 Dilute Nitric Acid — 1:1 (v⁄%). 


IS 15573 : 2018 


M-1.2.2 Dilute Phosphoric Acid — 1:1 (v/). 
M-1.2.3 Potassium Periodate — AR grade powder. 
M-1.2.4 Concentrated Sulphuric Acid — AR grade. 


M-1.2.5 Standard Manganese Solution — Dissolve 
0.3076 g of manganese sulphate monohydrate 
[MnSO,.H,O(AR)] in water, add 1 ml of concentrated 
sulphuric acid, AR grade, and make up the volume to 
1 000 ml in a volumetric flask. Dilute 10 ml of this 
solution to 1 000 ml. One millilitre of this solution is 
equivalent to 0.001 mg of manganese (as Mn). 


M-1.3 Procedure 


Weigh accurately 1g of sample and transferred to 100 ml 
beaker, dissolve in 30 ml of water and 5 ml of dilute 
nitric acid, heat to boil. Add 10 ml of dilute phosphoric 
acid and 0.6 to 0.8 g of potassium periodate. Again heat 
the solution to boiling for 10 min. Cool the solution to 
room temperature. Transfer the complete solution to a 
Nessler cylinder and makeup the volume to 100 ml mark. 


M-1.3.1 Separately carry out a control test using 5 ml 
of standard manganese solution in place of the sample 
and follow the procedure as prescribed at M-1.3. 


M-1.3.2 Visually compare the intensity of colour 
produced with sample (see M-1.3) with that of 
produced in the control test (see M-1.3.1). Same 
intensity of colour in both solutions indicates 
Manganese content in sample as 5 ppm. 


M-1.3.3 If colour intensity in the sample solution 
(see M-1.3) is higher than the control test (see M-1.3.1), 
dilute suitable quantity of sample solution (M-1.3) with 
water to 100 ml for comparison. If V ml of sample 
solution (see M-1.3) diluted to 100 ml matches with 
control test solutions (M-1.3.1), manganese content is 
evaluated by following equation: 


5x 100 
V 


M-1.3.4 If colour intensity of sample solution 
(see M-1.3) is less than control test solution 
(see M-1.3.1), dilute suitable quantity (Y ml) of control 
test solution (M-1.3.1) to 100 ml to matches with the 
colour intensity of sample solution (M-1.3). Manganese 
content in sample is evaluated by following equation: 


Mn (ppm) =

ANNEX N 
[Table 1, SI No. (viii) (g)] 
DETERMINATION OF CHROMIUM 


N-1 PRINCIPLE 


Chromium hexavalent is reduced to Chromium trivalent 
by boiling with potassium iodide and sodium sulphite 
followed by co-precipitation with aluminum hydroxide. 
Co-precipitated chromium along with aluminium 
hydroxide is dissolved in 1:1 sulphuric acid and 
chrominium is oxidized to hexavalent form by bromine 
water. Chromium is determined colorimetrically by 
reacting with diphenyl carbazide reagent, which gives 
a purple colour with chromium (VI). Alternatively 
Chromium is determined by Atomic Absorption 
Spectrophotometer (Referee method). 


12 


N-1.1 Reagents 
N-1.1.1 Sulphuric Acid — 1:1 (v/v) and 1:9 (v/v). 
N-1.1.2 Phosphoric Acid— 1:5 (v/). 


N-1.1.3 Diphenyl Carbazide Reagent — Dissolve 0.25 g 
of diphenyl carbazide and 0.4 g of phthalic anhydride in 
100 ml ethanol. The solution is stable for one month. 


N-1.1.4 Bromine Water 
N-1.1.5 Potassium Iodide Solution — 16 percent (w/v). 


N-1.1.6 Sodium Hydroxide Solution — 30 percent 
(w/). 


N-1.1.7 Neutral Sodium Sulphite Solution 
N-1.1.8 Potassium Dichromate — AR grade. 
N-1.1.9 Concentrate Hydrochloric Acid— AR grade. 


N-1.1.10 Aluminium Solution — Dissolve 1 g of 
aluminum metal in a little quantity of AR grade 
hydrochloric acid and dilute, transfer to 1 000 ml 
volumetric flask and make to the mark with distilled 
water. Shake well. 


N-1.2 Procedure 
N-1.2.1 Preparation of Standard Graph 


Weigh 0.283 g of dried potassium dichromate, dissolve 
in a little distilled water and dilute to 1 litre. One 
millilitre of this solution is equivalent to 0.1 mg of 
chromium (as Cr). Further dilute 10 ml of the above 
solution to 1 litre. One millilitre of the diluted solution 
is equivalent to 1 microgram of chromium. Take various 
volumes of the standard solution in separate beakers 
so as to give 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 microgram of 
chromium. Add 15 ml aluminum solution to each beaker 
and dilute to about 50 ml, add 30 ml 1 : 1 sulphuric 
acid and 2 ml bromine water. Further, add 30 percent 
sodium hydroxide solution dropwise till the colour 
disappears and add 2 drops in excess. 


Boil for 5 min and carefully add 1 : 1 sulphuric acid 
with continuous stirring till the bromine colour 
reappears and then add 0.5 ml of acid in excess. Again 
boil for about 20 min until bromine colour disappears. 
Check for presence of any bromine in solutions, cool 
and add 1 ml diphenyl carbazide solution and make up 
the volume to 100 ml, shake well. Allow to stand the 
solution for 15 min for full colour to develop and then 
read the percentage of transmission on a 
spectrophotometer at 540 nm. For adjusting 100 percent 
transmittance, use 35 ml water in place of standard 
solution and proceed in same manner as detailed above. 
Plot the graph for absorption/transmittance of light 
against the corresponding chromium concentrations. 


N-1.2.2 Weigh accurately about | g of the liquid (for 
solid about 0.33 g) sample in 100 ml beaker, dissolve 
in water and transfer in 500 ml volumetric flask, make 
up the volume to the mark with water. 


13 


IS 15573 : 2018 


Pipette out 100 ml of sample and transfer it in a 
1 000 ml beaker, add 20 ml of potassium iodide and 
20 ml of sulphuric acid and 100 ml of water. Boil for 
about 10 min. Add sodium sulphite in small portion to 
decolorize the sample. In case the solution turns brown 
on further boiling, continue adding sodium sulphite 
solution till the decolourization is stable and brown 
colour of iodine does not appear on boiling. 


Add sodium hydroxide drop-wise with continuous 
stirring and adjust the pH to 6.0 to 6.5. Allow to settle 
the precipitate. Decant the clear solution and collect 
the aluminum precipitate in a small beaker. Filter 
through a sintered glass crucible and wash once with 
water. Dissolve the precipitate by pouring 20 ml of 
boiling sulphuric acid solution (1 : 9) into the crucible, 
apply suction after 2 to 3 min and again wash with hot 
water. Collect the filtrate in 250 ml beaker. Add 4 ml 
bromine water and stir well. Decolourize the yellow 
colour with a few drops of sodium hydroxide solution 
and add 1 ml excess. Boil for 5 min and add 1: 1 
sulphuric acid until the brownish colour appears. Add 
2 ml of the acid in excess and boil again till brownish 
colour disappears. Cool and add 1 ml phosphoric acid. 
Add 1 ml diphenyl carbazide solution and make up the 
volume to 100 ml, shake well. Allow to stand the 
solution for 15 min for full colour to develop and then 
read the percentage of transmission on a 
spectrophotometer at 540 nm. From the standard graph, 
find out the concentration of chromium. 


N-1.3 Calculation 
Chromium (as Cr), ppm 


Mass in microgram of chromium in 100 ml x5 


Mass of sample taken for the test, in g 


N-2 REFEREE METHOD 


Determine Chromium content by Atomic Absorption 
Spectrophotometer as per method given in 
IS 3025 (Part 52). 


N-3 ALTERNATE METHOD 


Determine Chromium content by ICP-AES as 
prescribed in IS 3025 (Part 2).

ANNEX Q 
[Table 1, SI No. (ix)] 
DETERMINATION OF TOTAL ORGANIC CARBON 


Q-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


There are two analytical methodologies known as 
differential and direct method. The differential method 
uses the technique where TOC is calculated by 
subtracting Total Inorganic Carbon (TIC) from Total 
Carbon (TC) with the residual value being that of TOC. 
This method is commonly used in samples with less 
than or equal quantities or similar sized TIC and TOC 
and is described here. 


Q-1.1 Apparatus 
Suitable Total Organic Carbon (TOC) Analyser 


Q-1.2 Reagents — Depending on the TOC analyser/ 
methodology type of required reagents may vary 
slightly. 


Q-1.2.1 Potassium Hydrogen  Phathalate 
(AR Grade) — dried at 120°C for 1 hr and cooled in 
desiccator before use. 


Q-1.2.2 Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH) (AR Grade) — 
1 N Solution in TOC free water. 


Q-1.2.3 Sodium Carbonate (AR Grade) 
Q-1.2.4 Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate (AR Grade) 


Q-1.2.5 Sodium Persulphate AR Grade — 
Thirty percent solution in TOC free water. 


Q-1.2.6 Acid — 3M Hydrochloric Acid or Ortho 
Phosphoric Acid 


Q-1.3 Total Carbon (TC) Standard Solution 
Weigh accurately 2.125 g potassium hydrogen phthalate 


14 


(Q-1.2.1) and transfer to 1 litre volumetric flask and 
make up to the mark with TOC free water. Label it as 
stock solution-1 000 ppm TC. Dilute this solution 10 
times with TOC free water to prepare 100 ppm TC 
solution. 


Q-1.4 Inorganic Carbon (IC) Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately 3.5 g of sodium hydrogen carbonate, 
which was previously dried for 2 h, at 280-290°C and 
cooled in desiccators. Also weigh out 4.41 g of sodium 
carbonate previously dried for 1 hr at 280-290°C and 
cooled in desiccators. Transfer the above weighed 
materials into one litre volumetric flask and make up 
to the mark with TOC free water. It gives 1 000 ppm 
IC standard solution. Prepare 100 ppm IC solution by 
diluting 1 000 ppm IC standard solution ten times. 


Alternately weigh accurately 4.41 g of sodium carbonate 
previously dried for 1 h at 280-290°C and cooled in 
desiccators. Transfer this into 1 litre volumetric flask 
and make up to the mark with TOC free water. It gives 
500 ppm IC standard solution. Prepare 50 ppm IC 
solution by diluting 500 ppm IC standard solution ten 
times. 


Q-1.5 Preparation of IC and TC Calibration 
Curves 


Generate the calibration curves for IC and TC 
separately using respective standard solution. From 
“Calibration curve properties” windows, select the 
calibration points, that is 10, 20, 50 and 100 ppm by 
auto solution. First insert the TC solution (100 ppm) 
and run the programme. After completing the four 
standards insert the IC solution ( 50/100 ppm) and run 


the programme simultaneously and complete the four 
standard of IC solution. Use these two curves for sample 
analysis. 


Q-1.6 Procedure (Differential Method) 


Procedures for testing TOC may vary depending on 
type/make of the instrument; thus two mostly used 
procedures A and B are mentioned and suitable can be 
selected as per methodology/manual of the used 
instrument. 


Procedure — A 


Weigh accurately of PAC sample (for liquid sample 5 g; 
for powder sample 2 g) into a beaker. Add 25 ml of 
demineralized (DM) water (conductivity < 1 Siemens) 
or boiled and cooled distilled water. Add gradually 1N 
sodium hydroxide or 1N hydrochloric acid to the solution 
to adjust final pH between 2 to 3. Cool the solution and 
make up the volume to 500 ml. Start the TOC analyzer 
and after furnace temperature reaches prescribed 
temperature as per instrument manual select ‘TOC’ 
method and the standard curve of TC and IC. 


IS 15573 : 2018 


Admit the sample into the instrument and start the 
analysis. First the instrument reads the TC value and 
then the instrument reads IC value and automatically it 
gives the TOC value which is the difference of TC and 
IC values. Note the reading of the instrument (Final 
TOC value) and calculate the TOC content of the 
sample either directly from the instrument or otherwise 
(TOC in ppm = Instrument reading x 500/M). 


Procedure — B 


Weigh accurately of PAC sample (for liquid sample, 
30 g; for powder sample 10 g) into a beaker. Dissolve 
powder sample in 25 ml of demineralized (DM) water 
(conductivity < 1 Siemens) or boiled and cooled 
distilled water. Make up sample/sample solution to 
50 ml with TOC free water in a volumetric flask. 


Feed weight of sample used in the instrument for auto 
calculation. Admit the sample into the instrument and 
start the analysis. The instrument reads the IC & TC 
values and automatically it gives the TOC value which 
is the difference of TC & IC values. Note the TOC 
value directly from the instrument. 


ANNEX R 
[Table 1, SI No. (x)] 
DETERMINATION OF INSOLUBLE MATTER 


R-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


Insoluble matter is determined by dissolving the 
material in water and filtration through tared Gooch or 
sintered G-4 glass crucible followed by weighing of 
dried residue of the crucible. 


R-1.1 Procedure 


Weigh accurately about 10 g of the material, transfer 
into a 400 ml beaker, add about 200 ml of freshly boiled 
distilled water, and boil the resulting solution for 15 
min. Filter the solution through a tared Gooch or 
sintered glass crucible G-4 under vacuum and wash 


15 


the residue with hot distilled water till free from soluble 
salts. Dry the crucible along with the residue to constant 
mass at 105-110°C. 


R-1.2 Calculation 


M,x100 
Insoluble matter, percent by mass = M 
where 
M, = mass of the residue, in g, and 
M, = mass of the material taken for the test, in g. 


IS 15573 : 2018 


ANNEX S 
[Table 1, SI No. (xi)] 
DETERMINATION OF pH 


S-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


Determination of pH of the solution by means of a 
suitable pH meter. 


S-1.1 Procedure 


Take 5 g of the material and dissolve in 100 ml freshly 
boiled and cooled distilled water. Determine the pH of 
solution by means ofa suitable pre-calibrated pH meter, 
using glass electrode. 


ANNEX T 
(Clause 7) 
SAMPLING OF POLYALUMINIUM CHLORIDE 


T-1 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS OF SAMPLING 


T-1.1 While drawing samples, the following precautions 
and directions shall be observed. 


T-1.2 Sample shall not be taken in an exposed place. 
T-1.3 The sampling instrument shall be clean and dry. 


T-1.4 Precaution shall be taken to protect the material 
being sampled, the sampling instrument and the 
container for samples from adventitious contamination, 
particularly from absorption of water (that is moisture 
from atmosphere). 


T-1.5 To draw a representative sample, the content of 
each container selected from sampling shall be mixed 
thoroughly by suitable means. 


T-1.6 The sample container shall be of such a size that 
these are almost completely filled by the sample. 


T-1.7 The sample shall be placed in clean, dry and air 
tight glass, PVC or polythene containers. 


T-1.8 Each sample container shall be sealed air-tight 
after filling, and marked with full details of sampling, 
the date of sampling and batch number, if any. 


T-2 SCALE OF SAMPLING 
T-2.1 Lot 


All the containers in a single consignment of the 
material drawn from a single batch of manufacture shall 
constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared to consist 
of different batches of manufacture, the batches shall 
be marked separately and the groups of containers in 
each batch shall constitute separate lots. 


16 


T-2.2 Samples shall be tested from each lot separately 
for judging the conformity of the material to the specific 
requirements. The number of containers (n) to be 
selected at random from lots at different sizes (V) shall 
be in accordance with Table 2. 


T-2.3 Thecontainer/packages shall be drawn at random 
from the lot, and to ensure randomness of sampling 
random number table (see IS 4905) may be used, if it is 
not available then following procedure may be adopted. 


Arrange all the containers in the lot in a systematic 
manner, and starting from any one, count them as 1, 2 
up to n where n is the integral part of N/n. Every 
nth container thus counted shall be included in the 
sample till the required number of containers specified 
in col 2 of Table 2 is taken out. 


Table 2 Number of Containers to be Selected for 
Sampling 
(Clauses T-2.2 and T-2.3) 


SI Lot Size Number of Containers to 
No. N be Selected 
n 

(1) (2) (3) 

i) Up to 25 3 

ii) 26 to 50 4 
ili) 51 to 100 5 
iv) 101 and above 7 


T-3 TEST SAMPLE AND REFERENCE SAMPLE 


T-3.1 Polyaluminium Chloride — Powder 


Scrap off upper layer (50 mm height) of the material 
from the top centre andthen take a sample. The quantity 


of the material so drawn shall be not less than 200 g 
and the mass of total material taken out shall not exceed 
1 kg. Mix rapidly all the sampled material to constitute 
the composite sample. 


Divide this composite sample into three parts. One of 
these three sets shall be marked for purchaser, another 
for the supplier and third for the referee. All these three 
samples should have proper label for easy 
identification. 


T-3.2 Polyaluminium Chloride — Liquid 
T-3.2.1 From Tank Cars or Tank Wagons 


T-3.2.1.1 Draw samples from each tank or tank wagon 
from different levels by suitable sampling instrument. 
The sample material so collected shall be mixed 
altogether constitute a composite sample of 1500 ml 
into a clean resistant glass bottle, after thoroughly 
mixing of the material, divide the material into three 
parts and transfer each part into a sample container and 
closed tightly and labeled giving full identification 
particulars. One of these shall be marked for the 
purchaser, another for the supplier and the third for the 
referee. 


T-3.2.2 For Container 


T-3.2.2.1 Draw representative portion from each 


17 


IS 15573 : 2018 


container selected as per the sampling plan (see T-2.1 
and Table 2). After thoroughly mixing of material of 
the container, take out about 500 ml from each selected 
container. The sample material drawn from different 
container shall be mixed thoroughly altogether to 
constitute a composite sample. Divide the material into 
three parts and transfer each part to a sample container 
and closed tightly and labeled them giving full 
identification particulars, one of these shall be marked 
for the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third 
for the referee. 


T-3.3 Referee Sample 


T-3.3.1 The referee sample (T-3.1, T-3.2.1.1 
and T-3.2.2.1) shall bear the names of the purchaser 
and the supplier. It shall be used in case of dispute 
between the two. It shall be kept at a place agreed to 
between the purchaser and the supplier. 


T-4 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERION FOR 
CONFORMITY 


T-4.1 Tests for all the requirements of this standard 
shall be conducted on the composite sample. 


T-4.2 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the 
requirements of the standard if the composite sample 
satisfies all the tests given in T-4.1. 


Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CHD 13 (10731).
